title: Embeddings & Latency Economics: Enterprise Benchmark Dossier
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a concise, decision-ready benchmark dossier comparing candidate open and hosted embedding+generation stacks on cost-per-query, 95th-percentile latency at target QPS, and semantic stability for regulated verticals (finance, health, legal). This is explicitly intended to inform Dedicated capacity recommendations, pricing levers for enterprise deals, and fallbacks for Private deployments.

Background: Sales and Solutions have escalated multiple RFPs where latency SLAs and deterministic embedding quality are gating factors. We need a repeatable, impartial benchmark that ties model/quantization/serving configuration to real dollar cost and observed embedding drift across versions. The deliverable should make tradeoffs transparent for sales negotiations and product roadmap prioritization.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark matrix with at least 6 model+quantization+serving combos (open and hosted) with uniform test harness
Cost-per-1M queries estimate derived from Redwood runtime metrics and cloud pricing assumptions
95th and 99th percentile latency measured at representative QPS profiles (10, 100, 500), with variance bands
Embedding stability score (cosine drift over small prompt perturbations) and downstream retrieval accuracy delta for two vertical datasets
Executive one-pager with clear recommendation: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for each vertical and typical contract size
deliverables: CSV benchmark matrix (model, quant, runtime-config, cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput)
Notebooks used for embedding stability experiments and retrieval evaluation
Confluence dossier summarizing methodology, assumptions, raw logs, and sales-facing one-pager
Stakeholder readout slide deck and recording
data_sources: Vertical test corpora (finance q/a subset, anonymized clinical notes, legal precedents) - internal dataset repo
Runtime telemetry (token counts, GPU-hours) - observability console export
Cloud price sheets (GCP/AWS/Ops reserved pricing assumptions) - pricing model v2 spreadsheet
methods: Controlled synthetic load tests at target QPS profiles using Redwood load-harness
Embedding stability: compute cosine similarity across seeded perturbations and retrain-agnostic noise
Retrieval regression: measure avg. precision@10 using domain ground truth sets
Cost model: combine observed GPU-hours / throughput with amortized infra and software license costs to estimate cost-per-1M queries
risks: Benchmark variance due to noisy cloud spot capacity during peak runs
Model license restrictions that prevent publicizing certain numbers for sales collateral
Data sensitivity: health/legal datasets require scrubbing and legal sign-off before export
Availability of runtime kernel optimizations for certain quantized configs may change results mid-project
dependencies: ENG-62109 (runtime instrumentation for per-request GPU-time breakdown)
PM-74123 (enterprise procurement requirements for regulated verticals)
